$comment: What's new? drafts in English, by the id of each draft in data/news.json. An entry published from a draft unchanged shows this text to English players; an entry the author wrote or changed is translated by machine (src/server/news.js).

0.1.39.title: Version 0.1.39
0.1.39.body:
- In the Settlement, above the board, there is a “Brotherhood standings” bar. Folded, it shows each Brotherhood's standing.
- Unfolded, it shows the points, a bar to the next standing, what the current standing gives and what the next one will add.

0.1.40.title: Version 0.1.40
0.1.40.body: - On a computer the whole Settlement board fits on the screen without scrolling. The title and the Brotherhood bar stand beside it.

0.1.41.title: Version 0.1.41
0.1.41.body:
- In the Trade between players you can give wood, stone and iron ore: the offer has a “Camp resources” part under the gold.
- At Jagna's and Wszebor's, the “Sell” tab shows icons of herbs, potions and materials next to their names.

0.1.42.title: Version 0.1.42
0.1.42.body:
- The Brotherhood of Smiths gives more: a cheaper Anvil (up to 20% of the gold), a faster Workshop (up to 20%) and more items made one rarity higher (up to +4 percentage points).
- The Merchants' Company gives more: a lower Marketplace fee (down to 0.2%), auctions up to 48 hours and up to 5 items at the travelling merchant's.
- The “Brotherhood standings” panel shows the new benefits at each standing.

0.1.43.title: Version 0.1.43
0.1.43.body:
- The game's news now shows in a “What's new?” window when you enter the game, each entry once.
- The scroll icon in the top bar, next to the Settings, also opens earlier entries.

0.1.44.title: Version 0.1.44
0.1.44.body:
- A new Steady Scroll: when an upgrade on the Anvil fails, the item keeps its level. It works from +1 and can be used together with a Ward Scroll.
- The smith in the Forge sells the Steady Scroll for 1000 gold and the Ward Scroll for 2000 gold. Both are cheaper with the Brotherhood of Smiths.
- In the Workshop the Steady Scroll is made from Crafting level 10: 5 Fittings and 30 minutes.
- Both scrolls have icons.

0.1.45.title: Version 0.1.45
0.1.45.body:
- Rings, amulets and talismans taken apart at the Salvage Table now give mostly things for Jewelcrafting: setting ore and, from rare upwards, a gem one rarity lower. They give three times fewer parts for the Workshop.
- The gem and the ore come at once, the parts when the table is done.

0.1.46.title: Version 0.1.46
0.1.46.body:
- The Brotherhood of Herbalists gives more: Herbalism gathers up to 20% more herbs, Alchemy brews up to 20% faster, and timed potions last up to 2 fights longer.
- The Brotherhood of Hunters gives more: up to 20% more materials from creatures, elites and champions up to 20% more often, and up to 8 percentage points more at the Tannery.
- The “Brotherhood standings” panel shows these benefits at each standing.

0.1.47.title: Version 0.1.47
0.1.47.body:
- Each new Brotherhood standing has a reward waiting: System Points (1, 2, 3 or 5) and a gift of the Brotherhood's goods. Claim it with “Claim” in the “Brotherhood standings” panel in the Settlement.
- Standings reached earlier give their rewards too, all at once.
- The narrator in the Forge now speaks of both scrolls.

0.1.48.title: Version 0.1.48
0.1.48.body:
- The “What's new?” window no longer opens by itself when you enter the game.
- When a new entry appears, the scroll icon in the top bar gets a yellow dot. The dot goes out once you open the list.

0.1.49.title: Version 0.1.49: the Stronghold
0.1.49.body:
- A Camp at level 10, with every building at its highest level, can be turned into a Stronghold. The change starts at the Cornerstone.
- The Stronghold gets stone walls and seven new buildings: the Training Yard, the Armoury, the Trophy Hall, the Watchtower, the System Altar, the Greenhouse and the Shrine.
- Each of them strengthens your character in its own way. Its screen says how.

0.1.50.title: Version 0.1.50
0.1.50.body:
- In the Guild, long parts fold under their titles: the Trial board, thresholds and chests, the week's contribution, requests, benefactors, offers and invitations.
- Under the title of a folded part you see in short what it holds, e.g. how many trials are left to take.
- Your phone remembers which parts you folded.

0.1.51.title: Version 0.1.51: harder explorations
0.1.51.body:
- From level 11 the creatures in the newest place are stronger. A long exploration into the newest place may end in fainting.
- Companions and a party help a lot.
- Lower places are as they were. Check the “Threat” before you set out.

0.1.52.title: Version 0.1.52: harder with companions too
0.1.52.body:
- From level 30 the newest place is harder with companions too. The longest exploration sometimes ends in fainting.
- Without companions the newest place is now very hard. One place lower is safer.
- Check the “Threat” before you set out.

0.1.53.title: Version 0.1.53: Guild Trials every day
0.1.53.body:
- Guild Trials no longer need taking: all the trials on the board count at once, from the moment they appear.
- On Monday the board has 4 trials, and 2 new ones come every day.
- At most 2 of your trials count towards the guild bar for each day of the week. Those done beyond that will count on the following days.
- The bar has 6 thresholds, and the last two give bigger chests.
- This week the bar counts every trial done, with no daily limit.

0.1.55.title: Version 0.1.55: resource buildings up to level 20
0.1.55.body:
- In the Stronghold you can build the Sawmill, the Quarry, the Mine and the Midas Pond up to level 20.
- Each level adds as much as before, so at level 20 a building gives twice as much as at level 10, and its storehouse holds 40 hours of production.
- At level 20 a building gets a new look.
- Levels 11–20 cost as many resources as level 10, and a little more gold and time with each level.

0.1.56.title: Version 0.1.56: the Trial Hall and the Wanted
0.1.56.body:
- The Settlement has a Trial Hall. Once a day, for free, you can take its trial: three fights with the creatures of the next place, its elite among them. Pass it, and you may enter that place for good before your class level allows.
- On the Order Board the headman puts up wanted posters every day: three for named kinds of creatures and one for an outlaw. Take a poster, and on an exploration in that place you will meet the wanted one more often.
- For defeating the wanted one the headman pays in gold and Time Points, and the Brotherhood of Hunters shows its favour. A creature leaves a trophy, an outlaw rare loot.
- Guild Trials have a seventh threshold: the highest chest waits once all members have done all the week's trials.

0.1.57.title: Version 0.1.57: monthly quests
0.1.57.body:
- The narrator has monthly quests: a third tab next to the daily and weekly ones.
- Five quests for the whole month. The same explorations and work count as in the daily and weekly quests.
- The chest for all of them: +240 Time Points, +50 System Points and gold by your character's level.
- This month's quests fit the days left in it.

0.1.58.title: Version 0.1.58: the Order Board in tabs
0.1.58.body:
- The Order Board has two tabs: Orders and Wanted. There is less scrolling.
- A yellow dot on a tab shows that an order is waiting there to be handed in, or a reward to be claimed.

0.1.59.title: Version 0.1.59: the Guild Hall and harder explorations
0.1.59.body:
- The Guild has a Hall: a new tab with four buildings. The Banner gives more XP from explorations, the Treasury more gold, the Guild Forge cheaper upgrades on the Anvil, and the Scouts' Lodge rarer items more often.
- Each member pays gold and camp resources into a chosen building. The bonuses work for all the guild's members. The leader and deputies can mark the buildings worth saving for first.
- From character level 10 less HP comes back after a fight on an exploration, and from level 30 the creatures on explorations are stronger.
- The Exploration options have a Hard exploration box: stronger creatures, and in return +50% XP and gold.
- The bag shows how many Ward Scrolls and Steady Scrolls you have.

0.1.60.title: Version 0.1.60: Mercenaries in the Tavern
0.1.60.body:
- From level 25 you can put your character up for hire in the Tavern for a few hours, at your own price per hour of exploration.
- Another player takes the mercenary on one exploration, in place of one companion. The mercenary fights with all of their gear, and the pay waits for them in the Tavern when the exploration ends.
- A character up for hire does not set out, does not work in professions and does not change gear. You can take the notice down as long as no one has hired you.
- You choose a mercenary in the Exploration options: you pay up front, for the hours of the exploration.
- The description of the Wanted is now under “How does it work?”, and the quests fit on narrow phones.

0.1.61.title: Version 0.1.61: professions strengthen three times more
0.1.61.body:
- Each profession level now gives +3 to both of its stats instead of +1, for the levels gained earlier too.
- A mastered profession (level 100) gives 450 to each of its stats instead of 150.

0.1.62.title: Version 0.1.62: tagging on the chat
0.1.62.body:
- Type “@” and the start of a name, and the game suggests whom to tag. You can also tap “Tag” in a message's window or on a character's card.
- A message in which someone tagged you has a golden frame, and the Community shows a yellow dot until you read it.
- With notifications on, the tag also reaches your phone.

0.1.63.title: Version 0.1.63: three new outlaws
0.1.63.body:
- The headman's wanted posters now show Wojsław the Blaze, an arsonist with a fire pot, Masked Diana, a robber with two knives, and Ścibor the Digger, a grave robber with a spade.
- Wojsław sets things on fire, Diana is quick, and Ścibor is tough. The reward is the same as for the other outlaws.

0.1.64.title: Version 0.1.64: mercenaries straight from the Tavern
0.1.64.body:
- The Tavern has three tabs: Tankard, Companions and Mercenaries, so there is no more scrolling.
- The Mercenaries tab lists the characters waiting to be hired. “Hire” takes a mercenary to Combat, and you pay at “Set out”, for each hour of the exploration.
- You can now ask up to 100,000 gold per hour of exploration.
- The top bar on phones: the level and class fit in their frames again, even with a lot of gold, and the icons on the right stand closer together.

0.1.65.title: Version 0.1.65: the Guild Expedition and stopping a build
0.1.65.body:
- The Guild has a new tab: Expedition. Every week the guild goes through 7 stages, carried forward by the minutes of all its members' explorations.
- At the end of each stage a guardian bars the way. Everyone who added minutes attacks it 3 times a day. A defeated guardian gives a chest to everyone who added minutes, and the last one also leaves an item.
- In the Camp you can stop a build in progress: the gold and resources come back in full.

0.1.66.title: Version 0.1.66: the Salvage Table queue and Fame from the Expedition
0.1.66.body:
- At the Salvage Table each order in the queue has “Remove from queue”, and the whole queue “Remove all”.
- No penalty: materials and items come back, even from the order under way.
- Quests and Guild Trials give back what they counted from removed orders.
- Defeated guardians of the Guild Expedition give the guild Fame in the Ranking: 20 points for each and 50 for the seventh, up to 170 a week. Guardians defeated this week before this version count too.

0.1.67.title: Version 0.1.67: companions in events
0.1.67.body:
- Companions who went on the exploration with you also fight in the event fight at its end.
- Potions taken on the exploration, strengthening potions still at work and trophies work in the event fight too.
- On narrow phones the labels in the bottom bar and the resource names in the Camp fit in full. On a computer locked menu items are no longer cut off.

0.1.68.title: Version 0.1.68: fixes and companion standings
0.1.68.body:
- Salvage Table work counts towards quests and Guild Trials only once the order is done.
- Companions have their own relation standings: Distance, Comradeship, Trust, Friendship and Comrades in arms.
- The Trial Hall pays for an elite as for an elite and gives twice as many materials.
- “Stop the build” gives back exactly what was paid.
- Coming back to a guild in the same week no longer raises the thresholds of the Trials or the stages of the Expedition.
- A character up for hire as a mercenary has no attack dot at the Beast and the Expedition.
- The day's wanted posters do not change until midnight, and a poster your character set out with cannot be dropped on the way.

0.1.69.title: Version 0.1.69: a Party from level 10 and marching together
0.1.69.body:
- You can found a Party from character level 10, not 25.
- On a party exploration you walk side by side in Combat: each in their own look, on their own mount, with their aura, trails and familiar.
- The Guild tabs stand in two lower rows, so there is more room for the names.

0.1.70.title: Version 0.1.70: new narrator explanations
0.1.70.body:
- The narrator tells of the Mercenaries in the Tavern, the wanted posters on the Order Board, the Trial Hall, the Guild Expedition and the Stronghold when you go there for the first time.
- With a slow internet connection the narrator's hints are no longer lost.
- The explanations of Crafting and Mining wait until you come back from an exploration.

0.1.71.title: Version 0.1.71: jewellery for companions
0.1.71.body: - Companions now wear an amulet and a ring, not just a talisman. You put them on in the Camp, in the Quarters, with “Equip from bag”.

0.1.72.title: Version 0.1.72: the System Collector
0.1.72.body: - In the Camp, by the Account Chest, the System Collector floats. For 10,000 gold, once and for good, it gathers resources from the Camp's storehouses by itself when they fill up, even while you are away.

0.1.73.title: Version 0.1.73: fainting and companions' jewellery
0.1.73.body:
- Fainting wipes out the exploration: everything from it is lost, that is XP, gold, resources, materials and items, and an XP penalty comes on top. Check the “Threat” before you set out.
- A companion wears one piece of jewellery: an amulet, a ring or a talisman. If yours wore several, they keep the one put on last, and the rest went back to your bag.

0.1.74.title: Version 0.1.74: the Ranking without needless dots
0.1.74.body: - In the Ranking “…” now stands only where the list really skips places. When your place is just below the top ten, the list runs without a break.

0.1.75.title: Version 0.1.75: companions on the road
0.1.75.body:
- Companions from the Quarters who go on the exploration with you also walk beside your character on the Combat screen.
- The “Skip the explanation” button is smaller and no longer covers the narrator's words.

0.1.76.title: Version 0.1.76: the mercenary on the road and an even line
0.1.76.body:
- The mercenary from the Tavern walks beside your character on the Combat screen, in their own look and on their own mount.
- Companions and the mercenary walk level with your character, and when you ride, those on foot are smaller and tread the same path as the hooves.
- The companions' walks no longer flicker with grey specks on the outline: every frame was checked pixel by pixel.

0.1.77.title: Version 0.1.77: explanations you can skip
0.1.77.body:
- In the Settings, under “Narrator's voice”, there is a “Skip the narrator's explanations” switch. It works for all the characters on the account: the narrator does not explain new tabs and places, and a new character starts without the introduction.
- Tap the gem on an item's card to see what it gives. A gem raises all the item's values.
- The Raven and the Will-o'-the-Wisp no longer cover what your character holds in the portrait.
- When you ride, those walking beside you are smaller, as next to a real horse.
- Companions on the road have a black outline in every frame of their walk.

0.1.78.title: Version 0.1.78: a screenshot in a report
0.1.78.body: - In “Report a bug” in the Settings you can attach a screenshot from your phone's gallery. Only the game's author will see it.

0.1.79.title: Version 0.1.79: fixes
0.1.79.body:
- Explanations skipped with the “Skip the narrator's explanations” switch no longer come back when you open the game again.
- An old report of setting a gem shows on the item's card what the gem gives.

0.1.80.title: Version 0.1.80: the narrator without hold-ups
0.1.80.body:
- The narrator's explanations no longer stall when you set out on the next exploration straight from the report. The Settlement, the Towers and other parts will come in their own time.
- The narrator's card about a new level shows after the report, not over it.
- The narrator speaks of the Guild Expedition right after you tap its tab.
- When the narrator asks you to read the System's words in the Professions, “How does it work?” unfolds by itself.

0.1.81.title: Version 0.1.81: small fixes
0.1.81.body: - The “E-mail” label in the Settings no longer breaks on a phone next to a long address.

0.1.82.title: Version 0.1.82: Tier VI items
0.1.82.body:
- From class level 100, 22 new Tier VI items await, from the Flamberge to the Lunula. They drop on explorations from the Old Diggings on, and you will also find them in the weekly chest, at the travelling merchant's and in the Games Parlour.
- Their Workshop and Gem Workshop patterns are revealed at Crafting and Jewelcrafting level 100, and taking an item apart teaches its pattern earlier.
- The Encyclopedia has a Tier VI section with six sets. Each full set gives a chest: 6250 gold, 160 Time Points and 64 System Points.

0.1.83.title: Version 0.1.83: Jagna's rare recipes
0.1.83.body:
- Jagna the herbalist shares rare Alchemy recipes: three from the Trusted standing and three from the Friend standing, in your relation with her or in the Brotherhood of Herbalists' reputation. The recipes she has shared show in her “Buy” tab.
- An exploration's report names what a potion did, e.g. “Tough Skin was active in 2 of 4 fights.”
- The aura now glows around a character riding a mount, not just around the horse.

0.1.84.title: Version 0.1.84: comparing in the Quarters
0.1.84.body:
- In the Quarters “Equip from bag” shows the stats of each item. Tapping an item compares it with what the companion wears, and the “Equip” button puts it on.
- The bag's sorting buttons fit their labels even on a narrow phone.

0.1.85.title: Version 0.1.85: new narrator explanations
0.1.85.body:
- The narrator now explains the System Shop, the Guild tabs, the Party, the Hard exploration, the Account Chest, the System Collector, the Cornerstone and fainting, each at the first meeting.
- The narrator's cards about professions and about choosing a skill path sound new.

0.1.86.title: Version 0.1.86
0.1.86.body: - Preparations for the English version of the game. For now it works only on the test version, and in the game everything stays in Polish.

0.1.87.title: Version 0.1.87
0.1.87.body:
- Two new lands of the Whispering Pines for levels 151–200: the Silent Wilds and the New Moon Depths. Ten places and 34 new creatures, among them the elites Robber Nightingale and Plague Maiden and the champions Night Huntsman and Moon-Eater.
- New ways of fighting: creatures hidden in the dark become a target only once they are left alone, and the Moon-Eater strikes the whole formation at once.
- The lands' traits: in the Silent Wilds bleeding lasts one turn longer, and in the New Moon Depths chill does.

0.1.88.title: Version 0.1.88
0.1.88.body: - Fixes to the English version of the game, which for now works only on the test version. In the game everything stays in Polish.

0.1.89.title: Version 0.1.89
0.1.89.body: - Preparations for the English version of the game: choosing the language when creating an account. For now English works only on the test version, and in the game everything stays in Polish.

0.1.91.title: Version 0.1.91
0.1.91.body:
- Companions from the Quarters now go with your character on the Quick Hunt and the Lightning Hunt too: they fight beside it and gain experience as on a regular exploration.
- On narrow phones the narrator's and the quests' parchment fits fully on the screen, and long place names no longer run out of the frame.
- The chat also turns English swear words into asterisks.

0.1.92.title: Version 0.1.92
0.1.92.body: - In the Quarters you can take a weapon, armour or jewellery off a companion: tap the item they wear and choose “Unequip”. The item goes back to the bag, and the slot stays empty.

0.1.93.title: Version 0.1.93
0.1.93.body: - The narrator's explanation on your first visit to the Guild Hall no longer zooms the screen out: it points at the first building.

0.1.94.title: Version 0.1.94
0.1.94.body: - Salvage Table: under the material you picked, you choose how many pieces to process, not just the whole stack.

0.1.95.title: Version 0.1.95
0.1.95.body:
- The Towers page fits on narrow phones.
- The rules of the Guild Beast now say that you attack it during an exploration too.

0.1.97.title: Version 0.1.97
0.1.97.body:
- The game is in English too. You change the language in the Settings (the cog) or on the sign-in screen.
- The chat has an English channel, and under a message in another language there is an “A→ Translate” button: machine translation, up to 100 a day.

0.1.98.title: Version 0.1.98
0.1.98.body: - Wanted: the description on the Order Board now says plainly that you meet the wanted only on a regular exploration, not on a Quick Hunt, a Lightning Hunt or a Party exploration.

0.1.99.title: Version 0.1.99
0.1.99.body: - In English the creatures of Polish legend have English names instead of a phonetic spelling (e.g. Licho is Misfortune and Strzyga is Shriekwing). Their affixes on items and the names of their materials changed too.

0.2.0.title: Version 0.2.0
0.2.0.body: - In English the narrator speaks with a voice of his own: a native English narrator.

0.2.2.title: Version 0.2.2
0.2.2.body:
- What's new? entries are in English too: those who play in English read them in their own language.
- The no-connection screen speaks the game's language.
- The link insightrpg.com/en shows an English description of the game in its preview and opens the game in English.

0.2.3.title: Version 0.2.3
0.2.3.body:
- The game has Terms and a Privacy Policy (insightrpg.com/terms and insightrpg.com/privacy), and the page insightrpg.com/delete-account explains how to delete an account. The links are on the sign-in screen and in the Settings.
- Insight is for people aged 16 or over: a new account confirms it when it is made.

0.2.4.title: Version 0.2.4
0.2.4.body: - You can collect up to 30 Gifts from friends a day instead of 10. Each still gives a Time Point and gold or resources.

0.2.6.title: Version 0.2.6
0.2.6.body:
- New from character level 5: the System Portals, in the Combat tab. There are six: the Gold, Wood, Stone, Ore, Material and Parts Portals, and in each a win brings you only its own loot.
- You fight for the next stages as often as you like, even during an exploration, and your companions from the Quarters can come along. A win opens the next stage, up to your level (100 stages for now). The creatures are stronger than on explorations.
- A win and a sweep of a cleared stage give about as much as 45 minutes of an exploration at that level. You sweep with no fight, 5 times a day in each portal.

0.2.7.title: Version 0.2.7
0.2.7.body:
- The Towers now bring you much more. A win gets you as much gold as two hours of exploring at the floor's level, several times a Portal sweep.
- Every win also gives 3 materials of the floor's creatures, rarer the higher the floor: legendary and mythic from floor 50, divine too from floor 150.
- With a 15% chance a win gives an item of your class at the floor's level, epic or rarer. The Tower card shows the loot for the floor you pick.
- The Portals have their own backdrops, and their progress starts anew: in each portal you fight for stage 1 again.

0.2.8.title: Version 0.2.8
0.2.8.body:
- The narrator tells you about the Portals as soon as they open (from character level 5), in Polish and in English.
- A portal is now its picture with its name: tap it to see its stage, its fight and its sweep. No circles and no land names. A closed portal is a low strip, so the whole list fits without scrolling.
- At the top of the Portals there is "Sweep all": one tap uses all of today's sweeps in every portal.
- "Change character" is higher up in the Settings, above "Report a bug".

0.2.9.title: Version 0.2.9
0.2.9.body: - After a win in a Portal, the top of the report has "Fight for stage": the next stage at once, without going back to the list, if your character's level already allows it.

0.2.10.title: Version 0.2.10
0.2.10.body: - The top of the Character tab shows all your characters as small portraits: one tap and you play another. A yellow dot means that character has a report waiting.

0.2.11.title: Version 0.2.11
0.2.11.body:
- The Towers anew: floor 1 is level 50, and each next floor is one level higher. You can climb up to the floor of your own level.
- The System made the Towers' creatures twice as strong: they hit twice as hard and have twice the HP. Loot follows the floor's level, so even the first floor gives level 50 rewards.
- Tower progress starts over: chests and champions' trophies wait on their floors again, and today's entries are full. Nothing you have already won is taken away.

0.2.12.title: Version 0.2.12
0.2.12.body:
- You open the Towers' floors by climbing: every floor you conquer opens the next one, whatever your character's level.
- The Towers' creatures are now three times as strong: they hit three times as hard and have three times the HP.

0.2.13.title: Version 0.2.13
0.2.13.body: - The Cleric has a new portrait, with a clear face.

0.2.14.title: Version 0.2.14
0.2.14.body: - Gift code 50 for fifty accounts in the game: 50 System Points, 100 Time Points and 5000 gold. Enter it in the Settings, under "Gift code". It works until December 4 inclusive.

0.2.15.title: Version 0.2.15
0.2.15.body: - Gift code 1111, on November 11 only: 11 System Points, 111 Time Points and 1111 gold. Enter it in the Settings, under "Gift code". It works from midnight to midnight, Polish time.

0.2.16.title: Version 0.2.16
0.2.16.body: - Salvage Table: on the Parts tab the descriptions fit their frames again, and the piece counts no longer cover the text.

0.2.17.title: Version 0.2.17
0.2.17.body: - The Basilisk has a new look: the king of snakes in a crown of spikes, no longer with a rooster's head.

0.2.18.title: Version 0.2.18
0.2.18.body: - The Party Tower is now as hard as the Solo Tower: the System makes the creatures stronger as many times over as there are fighters on the party's side. Party Tower progress starts anew, and the rewards you won stay with you.

0.2.19.title: Version 0.2.19
0.2.19.body: - Towers: no more choosing a floor. The character always enters the first floor not yet won: a win leads up, and after a loss the same floor waits.

0.2.20.title: Version 0.2.20
0.2.20.body:
- Quick Hunts: 5 instead of 3, and once you use them all, they come back after 12 hours.
- Lightning Hunts: 5 instead of 3, and once you use them all, they come back after 6 hours.

0.2.21.title: Version 0.2.21
0.2.21.body: - Players online counter: a tab at the right edge of the screen. Tap the green dot and the number of players in the game slides out.

0.2.22.title: Version 0.2.22
0.2.22.body: - Guilds: a character already in a guild no longer sees invitations to other guilds, and cannot be invited.

0.2.23.title: Version 0.2.23
0.2.23.body:
- Hold “+” or “−” next to numbers (selling, stat points and more) and the number keeps changing by itself, faster and faster.
- Tapping buttons quickly no longer zooms the screen on a phone.

0.2.24.title: Version 0.2.24
0.2.24.body: - Guild Trials now ask for about twice as much: creatures, expedition minutes, herbs, potions, crafted items, materials and upgrades. Tower fights, Settlement orders and Requests stay the same. Trials opened from now on use the new numbers, the whole board from Monday.

0.2.25.title: Version 0.2.25
0.2.25.body:
- The System Collector now collects resources as they come, about once a minute, not only from full stores. Whoever already has one gets this at no extra cost.
- The Collector flies over the resources in the Camp, and their frames glow blue.

0.2.27.title: Version 0.2.27
0.2.27.body: - Over the character icons on the Character tab you now see how long each of them has left of what it is doing: an exploration, a profession's work or a mercenary service. When it ends, “Done” appears.

0.2.28.title: Version 0.2.28
0.2.28.body: - The timer over the character icons also counts the profession the System Avatar is working on. When two things run at once, you see the one that ends first.

0.2.29.title: Version 0.2.29
0.2.29.body: - Gift code 100 for a hundred characters in the game: 10 System Points, 100 Time Points and 1000 gold. Enter it in the Settings, under “Gift code”. It works until 5 December inclusive.

0.2.30.title: Version 0.2.30
0.2.30.body:
- Stats: “Spend by hand” next to “Spend by class” opens a slider for each stat. Set how many points go where and tap “Spend”.
- Skills: on a skill's card a slider adds as many Skill Points at once as you like.

0.2.31.title: Version 0.2.31
0.2.31.body: - In Combat under the threat: “The threat is the chance of defeat during the exploration.”

0.2.32.title: Version 0.2.32
0.2.32.body: - A lost exploration is now called a defeat, not fainting: in the report, the Journal, at the Shrine and in the description of the Fern Flower draught.

0.2.33.title: Version 0.2.33
0.2.33.body: - After the first lost exploration, the narrator now speaks of a defeat, just like the text.

0.2.34.title: Version 0.2.34
0.2.34.body: - The TIGER gift code (500 System Points) works a week longer, until 16 November inclusive. Enter it in the Settings, under “Gift code”.

0.2.36.title: Version 0.2.36
0.2.36.body:
- Marketplace: a “Log” tab with what your character sold, bought and won at auction, and the “For me” and “My bids” filters.
- Character: tapping an equipment slot shows the bag's items for that slot, with a comparison.
- Dismantling Table: the picked item is highlighted and described. The “Favourite” star in the item card keeps it from being dismantled, sold, thrown away or handed in for a Settlement order.
- A gem in an item that breaks on the Anvil, is dismantled, sold, thrown away or handed in for a Settlement order goes back to your minerals.
- Weeks of the year: each week gives a small bonus, e.g. +5% gold from fights. A bar above Combat tells you which week it is.
- Fame Points for explorations, professions, quests and more, in a new “Fame” tab in the Community. The top three accounts of the week share 150 System Points, and first place has a golden name for a week.
- The Party Tower also with companions from the Quarters, without a Party.
- Party: a member with a waiting report sets out with the party, and the report is claimed on its own.
- The System Avatar now gives a quarter of the character's experience and a quarter of the profession's progress.
- Wanted outlaws come from lower lands, and on a Party exploration you can meet an outlaw from anyone's poster in the party.
- Guild: a Guild Chest for items for everyone or for one member. Names at the Guild Beast open the character card.
- Ranking with 50 places a page and a “My place” button. Friends from the highest level, with the time of their last visit.
- Weekly quests ask for twice as much and give one and a half times more; monthly ones ask for four times as much and give twice as much. The new numbers start with the next week and month.
- Portals: the highest stage won shows next to each name.
- Settings: the game's music can be turned off so you can listen to your own. A Discord button sits by the Community and in the Settings.
- Fix: a party member always sees being on the exploration.

0.2.37.title: Version 0.2.37
0.2.37.body: - The Shadow is stronger: levels of the Shadow, the Assassin and the Kingslayer now give Vitality instead of Strength, which the class never used, so the character has more health. Execution and Beheading strike every third move instead of every fourth.

0.2.38.title: Version 0.2.38
0.2.38.body:
- The Arena is open in the Settlement from character level 25: duels with other players' characters, with a ranking and weekly rewards. Armour and reflected damage count only in part there, the same for every class.
- Weaker evolution paths are stronger on explorations. Elementalist: Fire Burst scorches the other enemies harder. Arcanist: the elemental hits harder and stays longer. Druid: the ent and the bear hit harder. Bastion: Shield Wall also raises its damage.
- Shadows that put points into Strength got them back to spend again, since Strength gives this class nothing.

0.2.39.title: Version 0.2.39
0.2.39.body: - Chat bubble: on a phone, a round chat button floats over the game. Tap it and the chat opens on its own screen. Drag it with your finger to another spot by the edge, or drop it on the × to hide it. Turn on “Chat bubble” in the Settings to bring it back.

0.2.40.title: Version 0.2.40
0.2.40.body:
- The chat is no longer among the Community's tabs. On a phone you open it with the round button over the game, and on a computer it sits in the column at the side. The bell for muting notifications now stands next to the chat's title.
- “Private message” on a character's card opens the conversation in the chat right away.

0.2.41.title: Version 0.2.41
0.2.41.body:
- The stats show what a whole stat gives, not one point. Tap a stat to see, for example: “Dexterity 690 now gives: damage +92.2%, dodge +16.2%, speed +1.01”.
- Arena: the last fight no longer plays by itself. You see its result, and “Watch the fight” opens the replay.

0.2.42.title: Version 0.2.42
0.2.42.body:
- The Arena has a new look: its picture, your rating on a plaque, the day's fights as crossed swords, and the last fight's result as a badge with “Watch the fight”.
- Shadows before evolution are evened out, the same on explorations and in the Arena: Shadow Dance protects for 3 enemy blows instead of 5, and Poisoned Blade poisons more often (45–65% of blows instead of 30–50%).

0.2.43.title: Version 0.2.43
0.2.43.body: - Arena fights take place on the arena's sand: the fight's replay has its own background.

0.2.44.title: Version 0.2.44
0.2.44.body: - Once you have the Settlement, an item's card has an “Enchant at the Enchantress” button. It takes the item straight to her workshop, where the affix and element enchantments open on it right away.

0.2.45.title: Version 0.2.45
0.2.45.body: - The Quarters have a 3rd level: a timber hall with a third bed. You can recruit a third companion, but at most two still go on explorations, and the third waits in the quarters as a reserve.

0.2.46.title: Version 0.2.46
0.2.46.body:
- Arena: a “Reroll rivals” button under the rivals. 5 times a day you can draw other rivals with a similar rating, and it does not use up a fight.
- Arena: “Recent defences” shows your character's last 10 defences. Watch any of them with “Watch the fight”, from the defender's side.

0.2.47.title: Version 0.2.47
0.2.47.body: - Towers: while the character is on an exploration, the note is short: “The character is on an exploration. You can enter the Towers once it returns.”

0.2.49.title: Version 0.2.49
0.2.49.body: - Hermit's Hut: Time Points for gold, up to 30 a day, 3000 gold each. You can buy them during an exploration too.

0.2.50.title: Version 0.2.50
0.2.50.body: - System Shop: a new Outfits tab. The Night Raven Cloak for the Shadow and the Forest Lord's Garb for the Archer, 800 System Points each. An outfit changes how the character looks at every evolution: on the portrait, in fights, on the march and in the saddle, always in the character's skin tone.

0.2.51.title: Version 0.2.51
0.2.51.body: - The bonus tile in the top bar (the flask with a number of fights): tap it and a list of the bonuses at work unfolds under it, with what they do and how many fights they have left.

0.2.52.title: Version 0.2.52
0.2.52.body: - Every land has a fight background of its own: in an exploration's report the fights take place on that land's ground, from the trampled earth of the Windfalls and the stone circle of the Stone Glade to the mud of the Black Bog and the gloom of the New Moon Depths.

0.2.53.title: Version 0.2.53
0.2.53.body: - The pony in the Combat scene is bigger: the rider no longer looks like an adult on a goat, and the pony is still stocky and lower than the horse.

0.2.54.title: Version 0.2.54
0.2.54.body:
- Guild wars: the Guild has a new War tab. Every week your guild fights a guild of a similar size, and battles of teams of 5 against 5 are fought every day at 20:00 (Polish time). Take your place in a team now: the first war starts on Monday, 16 November.
- For every battle you win you get gold and 2 System Points, and the guild that wins the war gets Fame and a war chest in the Guild Chest.
- A guild now holds 30 members, that is 6 teams.

0.2.55.title: Version 0.2.55
0.2.55.body: - The horse, the steed and the sabre-toothed tiger in the Combat scene are a little bigger, as the pony is now, so the rider sits on them in the right proportions.

0.2.56.title: Version 0.2.56
0.2.56.body:
- A new outfit in the System Shop: the Armour of Perun for the Warrior. Blackened armour with copper lightning, a wolf fur and a helmet with aurochs horns, on the portrait, on the march and in the saddle, at every evolution and in your character's skin tone.
- The horse in the Combat scene no longer shows a grey streak above its back that flashed every few steps.

0.2.57.title: Version 0.2.57
0.2.57.body: - On an iPhone the page no longer zooms in by itself after a tap on a list or after a window such as What's new? closes. Every text field and list now has a size at which the phone does not enlarge the page.

0.2.58.title: Version 0.2.58
0.2.58.body: - The Guild's War tab: with many members in the reserve, their portraits now wrap into several rows. The page is no longer wider than the screen, so on Android phones What's new? and other windows open normally, without the view sliding sideways.

0.2.59.title: Version 0.2.59
0.2.59.body: - Two new outfits in the System Shop: the Vestments of Dawn for the Cleric and the Robe of the Eclipse for the Mage. Your character wears them on the portrait, on the march and in the saddle, at every evolution and in their own skin tone.

0.2.62.title: Version 0.2.62
0.2.62.body: - The chat bubble is easy to bring back: once you hide it, a small speech bubble shows under the players online count by the right edge of the screen. Tap it and the chat bubble returns to its place.

0.2.63.title: Version 0.2.63
0.2.63.body: - Trading between players works from character level 20, on both sides.

0.2.64.title: Version 0.2.64
0.2.64.body:
- Seven new events on expeditions: Jagna in the Marsh, A Star from the Sky, The Ferryman, Dice by the Fire, Burnt Out, The Old Soldier, and a companion's errand from their past once your relationship reaches Trust.
- Helping the Settlement's residents in events raises your relationship with them, and saying no costs nothing.
- Gifts in the Settlement: once a day you can give each resident something they like. A resident who is your Friend leaves you a present once a week.

0.2.65.title: Version 0.2.65
0.2.65.body:
- From class level 125, 22 new Tier VII items await, from the Coronation Sword to the Torc. They drop on explorations from the Marsh Devil's Abyss on, and you will also find them in the weekly chest, at the travelling merchant's, in the Games Parlour, in the Towers, in the Guild Beast's chests, on the Guild Expedition and in the guild war chest.
- The Encyclopedia has a Tier VII section with six sets. Each full set gives a chest: 15,625 gold, 320 Time Points and 128 System Points.
- Professions now go up to level 200, and every level past 100 keeps strengthening both of the profession's stats. The bonus for mastering a profession at level 100 stays.
- Tier VII Workshop and Gem Workshop patterns are revealed at Crafting and Jewelcrafting level 125, and taking an item apart teaches its pattern earlier.
- The guild Exchange works from character level 20, on both sides, just like trading between players.

0.2.66.title: Version 0.2.66
0.2.66.body:
- The Marketplace is easier to search: each kind of goods has its own tab, and for items you can choose a class and a rarity. The search covers all the offers, not only those ending first.
- "For me" also shows what a chosen companion from the Quarters can equip now, and an unfolded item compares with what your character and every companion who can equip it wear.
- Sorting the offers: ending soon, cheapest or most expensive, by the price of a piece.
- Parties and companions: you no longer have to leave your companions in the quarters before you start or join a party. The game asks once, and while you are in a party your companions wait in the Quarters by themselves. After the party each goes back to how it was set.
- Training in the Quarters: "Train" raises a companion's level by one for 25 gold times the level they reach, up to three times a day and at most to your character's level minus 3. A companion does not train while out on an exploration.
- Guild Requests work from character level 20, on both sides, just like trading between players and the guild Exchange.

0.2.67.title: Version 0.2.67
0.2.67.body:
- Jagna from the marsh comes once, and then only the Drowned Maiden, even if you visit the Settlement in between.
- Settlement events (Jagna, the Drowned Maiden, companions' errands) come only once your character has the Settlement.
- A companion's errand in which you fight together closes whatever the fight's result. Win it and you get the next stage of your bond and a rarer item.
- A party left with only its leader and no invitation waiting ends, so the leader's companions go back on explorations at once.

0.2.69.title: Version 0.2.69
0.2.69.body:
- Arena: a fight sent just before midnight between Sunday and Monday no longer drops out of the week's table, and the Arena open in two tabs at once shows the right rivals.
- Guild wars: the Fame for a war won always reaches the week's ranking, and characters of one account on both sides of a war do not fight each other.
- Account Chest: the items of a removed character stay in the chest as items of another character.

0.2.70.title: Version 0.2.70
0.2.70.body:
- Exchange: trading many kinds of goods at once (such as a dozen or more materials) no longer fails.
- Guild Chest: items go in and come out from character level 20, as in the Exchange. You can always take your own item back.
- Gifts: in the week after the clocks change, they no longer disappear an hour early.

0.2.71.title: Version 0.2.71
0.2.71.body:
- Security fixes: daily limits (the Hermit's Time Points, daily quests, profession work) always count by the right day, also just before midnight.
- A gift code for one character works only once.

0.2.72.title: Version 0.2.72
0.2.72.body:
- Party: a report claimed at the moment someone in the Party skips the end of the exploration pays out once. A Party member's rumor from the Tavern waits for their own exploration.
- Trial chests and Expedition chests earned in a guild wait until the end of the next week, also after leaving the guild or after it ends. Trial chests from a former guild show in the Trials tab.
- The Guild Beast grows with everyone who joins the guild during the week, as the Trials and the Expedition do.
- A potion drunk at the same moment as another one or as claiming a report works properly, and several taps on “Build” at once pay once.
- A mercenary hired at the last moment of the offer gets their pay.

0.2.73.title: Version 0.2.73
0.2.73.body:
- Safer sign-in: the limit of password attempts holds also for attempts sent at once.
- Character and guild names: letters of one alphabet (Latin, Greek or Cyrillic), with no invisible signs. A name that only looks like someone else's can no longer be taken.
- Mails with a link: at most one a minute and five a day to one address, from any account.
- You can attach a screenshot to “Report a bug” once your e-mail is confirmed; the report itself you can send right away.
- The chat recognises links better, and failed translations go back to the daily pool within a sensible limit.

0.2.74.title: Version 0.2.74
0.2.74.body:
- Enchantress: with a choice of several affixes, the item gets the first one rolled at once, and your choice can swap it for another of them.
- The smith does not raise the rarity of an item whose affix choice is still waiting.
- The daily and weekly limits of the Settlement, the Stronghold, the Towers and the Portals work right at midnight too.
- Salvage Table: you cannot take the salvage of an item that taught a pattern off the queue while items are being made from that pattern.
- Fixes for gems of items sold when the bag is full, for putting items on, for test notifications and for Guild Requests after changing guilds.

0.2.75.title: Version 0.2.75
0.2.75.body:
- Selling, throwing away, equipping and upgrading an item, and setting a gem, always hit the item you chose, even when a new one arrives at the same moment.
- Fame Points from Sunday's last moment are no longer lost: they count toward the new week.
- A name you choose while the System renames blocked names stays yours, and offers on the Marketplace show the seller's current name.
- A name that looks like another character's is taken even when written in another alphabet.
- Two characters created at once for the last free place no longer leave the account without a character.

0.2.76.title: Version 0.2.76
0.2.76.body:
- Combat: when the guard of Unyielding, Unbending or Indomitable ends, armour no longer drops below what the armour tearing alone (Millstone, Curse of Decay) would leave.
- Combat: guards, shields and evades wake at once after a reflected blow too, and a fighter killed by a reflected blow strikes no more.
- Divine Protection no longer switches off Mana Mirror or Ice Armour.
- Frost Gust and Elemental Ray slow only those they hit.
- Fixed numbers on the Stats screen, on skill cards, in Advanced stats and on the fighters' cards in reports.
- The daily limits of the Arena, the Fire Spirit, the Scrapyard, the Merchant and the travelling merchant work right at midnight too.
- A character offered as a mercenary no longer fights in the Portals, and parts bought from others no longer count in the Encyclopedia.

0.2.77.title: Version 0.2.77
0.2.77.body:
- A Gift from a character below level 20 gives gold or resources by the sender's level.
- Donations to the Guild Hall's buildings from character level 20. Younger characters see the buildings and their bonuses.
- The land and level of the Guild Expedition count the members who played in the last 7 days.
- At most 20 sales a week at the Marketplace bring Fame. The gold comes as usual.
- The descriptions of the Caretaker and Grace traits say when healing removes harmful effects.

0.2.78.title: Version 0.2.78
0.2.78.body:
- The headman's wanted posters come from the highest place open to you and the two places below it, your newest land included. The bounty grows with the place's level.
- Today's wanted posters have been drawn anew. A poster already in your hand stays, with its own bounty.

0.2.79.title: Version 0.2.79
0.2.79.body:
- You can change your password in the Settings: “Password” → “Change”. The account's other devices are signed out.
- Forgot your password? The login screen has “I forgot my password”. A link to a new password comes to the account's confirmed e-mail address and works for an hour.
- By the Core: “The Core will be unlocked in one of the upcoming updates.”

0.2.80.title: Version 0.2.80
0.2.80.body:
- Account name: in the Settings you can set a name the chat shows before your character's name, e.g. “Wanderer (Radomira)”. It is shared by all the characters on your account, and you can change it at most once every 30 days.
- Changing the e-mail address now needs your current password.
- After a password change, the account's phones stop getting notifications until the game opens on them.
- A character's name or an account name can no longer look like someone else's through similar signs, such as the digit 0 for the letter o.

0.2.81.title: Version 0.2.81
0.2.81.body: - The Workshop and the Gem Workshop have no 5-piece cap and no time limit: order as many pieces as your parts, materials and bag room allow. For example, 20 common swords at Crafting level 1 are 10 hours of work.

0.2.82.title: Version 0.2.82
0.2.82.body:
- A Storeroom in the Workshop and the Gem Workshop: finished items and jewellery wait there outside your bag, with no limit on places. Mark them and put them in the bag, sell them to the scrap dealer or salvage them on the Salvage Table.
- A full bag no longer stops orders in the Workshop and the Gem Workshop: only parts and materials count.

0.2.83.title: Version 0.2.83
0.2.83.body:
- A party's exploration no longer sets out with the leader alone. When nobody in the party can go, the game says why, and the leader sets out alone only after unticking “With the party”.
- For now a party's explorations end in no events, so the members' reports are claimed by themselves when the party sets out again. Party events are on the way.
- “Set out again” in a leader's report takes the party along.
- The “With the party” box in Combat shows a member who has just come back by itself.

0.2.84.title: Version 0.2.84
0.2.84.body:
- The Account Chest now takes goods too: potions, herbs, materials, minerals and camp resources, with no limit. They are in the new “Goods” tab.
- The Account Chest opens at character level 20. Until then it has a padlock on it.
- The Encyclopedia does not count goods from another character, just as with items.

0.2.85.title: Version 0.2.85
0.2.85.body:
- Party events: a party's trip may end in an event for everyone who went. The leader chooses, and everyone gets the result in a separate report.
- If the leader does not choose within 12 hours, the party takes the safest way.
- Some choices give a bonus for the party's next trip: a shorter trip, or more XP or gold.
- A mimic may lurk in the “Buried Chest”.

0.2.86.title: Version 0.2.86
0.2.86.body:
- Wheel of Fortune: one free spin a day, at the lowest stake's odds.
- At the Tannery, in the “Sell” tab, material names show the colour of their rarity, as in the bag.

0.2.87.title: Version 0.2.87
0.2.87.body:
- The System Labyrinth from character level 30: in the Settlement, in the Trial Hall. A new labyrinth every day with three levels, and after the third, on the same day, the Hellish level. You choose your way through the chambers: fights, elites, treasures, springs, altars and a merchant. Wounds stay from fight to fight, and blessings last until the end of the day.
- The Labyrinth's guardians guard Artifacts. The first guardian you beat opens the Core in the Character tab: Artifacts are absorbed for good, and Core Shards upgrade them.
- A Tower champion's first defeat also gives an Artifact.
- In English, the names of places on the Settlement board no longer stick out past its edge.

0.2.88.title: Version 0.2.88
0.2.88.body: - An item the smith has reforged to a higher rarity says so on its card, on the Marketplace too: it cannot be reforged again. A buyer sees it before buying.

0.2.89.title: Version 0.2.89
0.2.89.body:
- The narrator explains the System Labyrinth: at character level 30 they lead you to the Settlement, to the Trial Hall, and show the map, the party's wounds, the day's levels and the rewards.
- On the Marketplace every item shows its Tier.

0.2.90.title: Version 0.2.90
0.2.90.body: - The System Labyrinth now sets its difficulty by the higher of two levels: your character's or your class's. Usually that is the class level, so the creatures are stronger, and a win gains you more gold and XP.

0.2.91.title: Version 0.2.91
0.2.91.body: - In the Labyrinth, the choice of a blessing and the merchant's wares open in a window as soon as you enter the chamber, with no scrolling back up the page.

0.2.92.title: Version 0.2.92
0.2.92.body: - The item verdict (the arrows in the bag and the line on the item card) counts attributes as “Spend by class” does: the ones your class does not need do not count at all, and the rest count by their weight. Weapon damage, armour and resistances count as before.

0.2.93.title: Version 0.2.93
0.2.93.body:
- A new card game in the Games Parlour: the System Deck (the “Cards” tab). Take the starter deck from Szczęsny, build a deck of 12 creature cards and play him at five tiers, for a stake or for practice. Win and you take double the stake, and beating a tier for the first time gives you a new card.
- Creatures you defeat on an exploration may leave their card: ordinary ones rarely, elites and champions more often. Another copy of the same card raises its level.
- Collection bonus: every 10 different cards give a permanent +1% XP and +1% gold from explorations, up to +15%.
- The Encyclopedia has a new “Cards” tab: every card by land, found and still unknown, with the collection bonus.

0.2.94.title: Version 0.2.94
0.2.94.body:
- Marketplace: a new “Tier” filter for items, next to class and rarity. It shows the items of one Tier and the class level they can be worn from. It works in “For me” too.
- Tavern: “New candidates” for gold, up to 3 times a week, each draw dearer than the last. Zbylut brings four other candidates, and the companions you hired stay.

0.2.95.title: Version 0.2.95
0.2.95.body:
- Combat: the wanted poster you hold now shows on the Combat screen: whom you hunt and where. A tap on the poster takes you straight to that place, and the place has a “Wanted poster” mark in its land. Once the quarry falls, the poster leads you to the headman for the reward.
- New versions now go live faster.

0.2.96.title: Version 0.2.96
0.2.96.body: - Guild Chest: an item's card compares it with what you wear and with what your companions wear, as on the Marketplace. The list also shows whether the smith has already reforged an item.

0.2.97.title: Version 0.2.97
0.2.97.body:
- Notifications: when they cannot be switched on, the game says why under the switch and what to do (permission in Chrome and in the phone's settings, incognito tabs, Google Play services). It also tries to fix the most common troubles by itself.
- “Report a bug” adds the state of notifications on the device, to find the cause more easily.

0.2.98.title: Version 0.2.98
0.2.98.body: - Fight speed ×4: the “Speed” button under a fight being played now goes 1× → 2× → 4×. The game remembers the chosen speed.

0.2.99.title: Version 0.2.99
0.2.99.body: - The game reloads into a new version also when you move between screens, not only when you come back to it from another app. Fixes reach you sooner.

0.3.0.title: Version 0.3.0
0.3.0.body:
- The third class evolution: at class level 200 every second form grows into a third. 15 new forms, among them the Horde Slayer, the Colossus, the Bowmaster, the Frost King, the Archdruid, the Prophet, the Lich and the Shadow Lord, each with its own portrait, walk and rider in every skin tone, a new trait and two new skills with icons and sounds.
- The points of the second form's skills come back to spend, and class levels 200 to 299 give a point each for the new skills.

0.3.1.title: Version 0.3.1
0.3.1.body:
- The Druid's Ent and the Archdruid's Ancient Oak have their own figures in fights.
- "Set out again" on a report stays above the bottom tabs, like "Set out" on a place's screen.
- A report with a level up lets you spend your free points at once: "Spend by class" or "Spend by hand".
- When creating a character, "Begin" is always at hand, with what is still missing beside it. On a computer the classes stand in two columns.
- Marketplace: when listing an item, tap it to unfold its full card with a comparison to the one you wear.

0.3.2.title: Version 0.3.2
0.3.2.body:
- Companions evolve: at their 50th, 100th and 200th level they take the form of the path of the first skill on their card by themselves, with its name, trait and two skills. A hired Cleric with Prayer for Health becomes a Healer and heals the whole party with Renewal. Their look stays their own, and those already at level 50 have evolved at once.
- The Storeroom in the Workshop and the Gem Workshop: the marked item shows a comparison with what the character wears in that place.

0.3.3.title: Version 0.3.3
0.3.3.body:
- Fights have new hit animations: a blow lands on its target with force, the target is knocked back, a crit flashes with "CRIT!", and the fight's last blow slows down. Every fight in the game looks like this. With Animations off (Settings) nothing shakes or slows down.
- The card game in the Games Parlour has animations: cards fly out and turn over on the table, blows come one by one with sparks, beaten cards crack, and the end of a match is a scene with Szczęsny and coins flying into your gold. Tapping the table ends a round's animation.

0.3.5.title: Version 0.3.5
0.3.5.body:
- The Labyrinth has a board of its own: the door in the Trial Hall opens it full screen. It shows every chamber of the level, the roads between them and your party walking to the chamber you pick.
- Fight platforms have a coloured ring: green is an easy fight, yellow an even one, red a dangerous one. The colour changes with your party, so wounds and blessings count too.
- Elites and treasures show how many Core Shards they give.

0.3.6.title: Version 0.3.6
0.3.6.body:
- The Guild tab has a new “Members' ranking” card. “Activity” shows how much Fame each member brought the guild this week or in all time. Tap a member to see where their Fame comes from: the Beast, the Expedition, Trials, Requests, the Exchange or War.
- “Donations” shows how much gold and resources each member gave to the Hall. Donations from before they were recorded stand together under the list.
- In the Hall, the “Who gave what” button opens those donations straight away.
- On narrow phones, the day's rewards at the Labyrinth's entrance are no longer cut off.

0.3.7.title: Version 0.3.7
0.3.7.body:
- The Labyrinth is easier: its creatures sit roughly halfway between the old Labyrinth and the latest one.
- After you collect an expedition's report, “Back” leads to the expeditions of the same place, not to the start of Combat.
- Another character's card shows the gem set in an item.

0.3.8.title: Version 0.3.8
0.3.8.body: - The locked Core says how to open it: defeat the first guardian of the System Labyrinth. The Labyrinth is in the Settlement, in the Trial Hall, from character level 30.

0.3.9.title: Version 0.3.9
0.3.9.body:
- Every fight you win on an exploration can give a card of a creature from a lower land, first one you do not have yet.
- Cards also drop in the Labyrinth, for work in a profession (1% for each hour, up to 10%), for attacks on the Beast and on the Guild Expedition's guardians, and for completed Guild Trials.

0.3.10.title: Version 0.3.10
0.3.10.body:
- After a lost fight in the Labyrinth you can start it again once a day: from level 1, with your party at full HP. It costs a lot of gold, and the rewards you gained earlier that day stay.
- An item card with a stone set in it shows each value without the stone and, beside it in brackets in the stone's colour, the value with it.

0.3.11.title: Version 0.3.11
0.3.11.body:
- The Labyrinth gets harder with every level: level 1 is easy, level 2 medium, level 3 hard and the Hellish level very hard.
- You can change the order of the Salvage Table's queue: hold ≡ by a waiting order and drag it to a new place. The order at work stays first, and the “Ready at” times are counted anew.

0.3.12.title: Version 0.3.12
0.3.12.body: - Once a day Szczęsny sells a pack of three creature cards from the lands lower than yours in the Games Parlour, for the gold of an hour of exploring at your level. Cards you don't have yet come first. You'll find the pack in the Cards tab, under your hero card.
